questions.question_text:
The area of a square is 𝑑. What is the area of the circle which has the diagonal of the
square as its diameter?
questions.explaination: For a square of area $d$, the side length is $s = \sqrt{d}$ and its diagonal is $s\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{2d}$. Since this diagonal is the diameter of the circle, the radius is $r = \frac{\sqrt{2d}}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{d}{2}}$. Hence, the area of the circle is $\pi r^2 = \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\pi d$.
questions.question_text_latex: The area of a square is $d$. What is the area of the circle which has the diagonal of the square as its diameter?

questions.question_text:
What would be the smallest natural number which when divided either by 20 or by 42 or
by 76 leaves a remainder of 7 in each case?
questions.subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, series
questions.explaination: The required number is $\text{LCM}(20, 42, 76) + 7$. Calculating prime factorizations: $20 = 2^2 \times 5$, $42 = 2 \times 3 \times 7$, $76 = 2^2 \times 19$. Thus $\text{LCM} = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7 \times 19 = 7980$. Adding the remainder 7 gives $7980 + 7 = 7987$.

questions.question_text:
What is the missing number in the following sequence?
2, 12, 60, 240, 720, 1440, _____, 0
questions.subtopic: Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, series
questions.explaination: Examining consecutive multipliers: $2 \times 6 = 12$, $12 \times 5 = 60$, $60 \times 4 = 240$, $240 \times 3 = 720$, $720 \times 2 = 1440$. Following this decreasing multiplier pattern, the next term is $1440 \times 1 = 1440$, and the term after is $1440 \times 0 = 0$.

questions.question_text:
Which one of the following is a closed form expression for the generating function of the
sequence {an}, where an = 2n + 3 for all n = 0, 1, 2,… ?
questions.subtopic: Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions
questions.explaination: The generating function is $G(x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty (2n + 3)x^n = 2\sum_{n=0}^\infty n x^n + 3\sum_{n=0}^\infty x^n$. Using the standard power series $\sum_{n=0}^\infty x^n = \frac{1}{1-x}$ and $\sum_{n=0}^\infty n x^n = \frac{x}{(1-x)^2}$, we obtain $G(x) = \frac{2x}{(1-x)^2} + \frac{3(1-x)}{(1-x)^2} = \frac{3 - x}{(1-x)^2}$.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following processor design characteristics.
I.
Register-to-register arithmetic operations only
II.
Fixed-length instruction format
III.
Hardwired control unit

Which of the characteristics above are used in the design of a RISC processor?
questions.explaination: RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) architectures feature load-store designs where arithmetic operations operate only on registers (I), fixed-length instruction encodings for streamlined pipelining (II), and hardwired control units for single-cycle instruction execution (III). Hence, all three characteristics I, II, and III are typical of RISC processors.

questions.question_text:
Let N be an NFA with n states. Let k be the number of states of a minimal DFA which is
equivalent to N. Which one of the following is necessarily true?
questions.explaination: By the subset construction algorithm, converting an $n$-state NFA to a DFA produces states that are subsets of the NFA states. Thus, the power set has $2^n$ possible states, ensuring that any equivalent minimal DFA has $k \le 2^n$ states.

questions.question_text:
The following are some events that occur after a device controller issues an interrupt while
process L is under execution.
(P) The processor pushes the process status of L onto the control stack.
(Q) The processor finishes the execution of the current instruction.
(R) The processor executes the interrupt service routine.
(S) The processor pops the process status of L from the control stack.
(T) The processor loads the new PC value based on the interrupt.
Which one of the following is the correct order in which the events above occur?
questions.subtopic: I/O interface: interrupt and DMA mode
questions.explaination: Upon receiving an interrupt, the processor finishes the execution of the current instruction (Q), saves the processor status and return PC onto the stack (P), loads the starting address of the ISR from the interrupt vector table (T), executes the ISR (R), and finally restores the saved status and resumes process $L$ (S). Hence the order is QPTRS.
questions.question_text_latex:
The following are some events that occur after a device controller issues an interrupt while process $L$ is under execution.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, nosep]
    \item[P.] The processor pushes the process status of $L$ on to the control stack.
    \item[Q.] The processor finishes the execution of the current instruction.
    \item[R.] The processor executes the interrupt service routine.
    \item[S.] The processor pops the process status of $L$ from the control stack.
    \item[T.] The processor fetches the new PC value from the interrupt vector.
\end{itemize}
Which one of the following is the correct order of events?

questions.question_text:
Consider a process executing on an operating system that uses demand paging. The average
time for a memory access in the system is M units if the corresponding memory page is
available in memory, and D units if the memory access causes a page fault. It has been
experimentally measured that the average time taken for a memory access in the process is
X units.

Which one of the following is the correct expression for the page fault rate experienced by
the process?

questions.question_text:
In an Entity-Relationship (ER) model, suppose 𝑅 is a many-to-one relationship from entity
set E1 to entity set E2. Assume that E1 and E2 participate totally in 𝑅 and that the cardinality
of E1 is greater than the cardinality of E2.

Which one of the following is true about 𝑅?

options.A: Every entity in E1 is associated with exactly one entity in E2.
options.B: Some entity in E1 is associated with more than one entity in E2.
options.C: Every entity in E2 is associated with exactly one entity in E1.
options.D: Every entity in E2 is associated with at most one entity in E1.

questions.explaination: In an ER diagram, a many-to-one relationship from $E_1$ to $E_2$ means each entity in $E_1$ is related to at most one entity in $E_2$. Total participation of $E_1$ requires that every entity in $E_1$ participates in at least one relationship. Combining these, every entity in $E_1$ is associated with exactly one entity in $E_2$.

Assume that $E_1$ has total participation in $R$, but $E_2$ has partial participation in $R$. Which one of the following statements is necessarily TRUE?

options_latex.D: Every entity in $E_2$ is associated with at most one entity in $E_1$.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following two tables and four queries in SQL.
Book (isbn, bname), Stock (isbn, copies)

Query 1: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B INNER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Query 2: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B LEFT OUTER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Query 3: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B RIGHT OUTER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Query 4: SELECT B.isbn, S.copies
FROM Book B FULL OUTER JOIN Stock S
ON B.isbn = S.isbn;

Which one of the queries above is certain to have an output that is a superset of the outputs
of the other three queries?
questions.subtopic: Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL
questions.explaination: Query 1 uses natural join (inner join), Query 2 uses left outer join, Query 3 uses right outer join, and Query 4 uses full outer join. A full outer join preserves all tuples from both relation $Book$ and relation $Stock$ (filling missing values with NULLs). Therefore, every tuple output by Query 1, Query 2, and Query 3 is guaranteed to appear in Query 4.

options_latex.A: Query 1 and Query 2 always produce the same number of rows.
options_latex.B: Query 2 and Query 3 always produce the same number of rows.
options_latex.C: Query 1 always produces the maximum number of rows among all queries.
options_latex.D: All rows from Query 1, Query 2, and Query 3 are always present in the result of Query 4.

Consider the following statements regarding the slow start phase of the TCP congestion
control algorithm. Note that cwnd stands for the TCP congestion window and MSS denotes
the Maximum Segment Size.
(i) The cwnd increases by 2 MSS on every successful acknowledgment.
(ii) The cwnd approximately doubles on every successful acknowledgement.
(iii) The cwnd increases by 1 MSS every round trip time.
(iv) The cwnd approximately doubles every round trip time.

Which one of the following is correct?
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: In TCP slow start, the congestion window (`cwnd`) increases by 1 MSS for each acknowledged segment. Consequently, when all segments in a flight are acknowledged, `cwnd` approximately doubles every round-trip time (RTT). Thus, statement (iv) is TRUE.

questions.question_text:
Two people, P and Q, decide to independently roll two identical dice, each with 6 faces,
numbered 1 to 6. The person with the lower number wins. In case of a tie, they roll the dice
repeatedly until there is no tie. Define a trial as a throw of the dice by P and Q. Assume that
all 6 numbers on each dice are equi-probable and that all trials are independent. The
probability (rounded to 3 decimal places) that one of them wins on the third trial is _____.
questions.explaination: On rolling two fair dice independently, the probability of a tie is $P(\text{tie}) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}$, and the probability of someone winning (no tie) is $1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. The game ends on the third roll if trials 1 and 2 are ties and trial 3 produces a winner: $P(\text{Trial 3}) = \left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \times \left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \times \left(\frac{5}{6}\right) = \frac{5}{216} \approx 0.0231$.
questions.question_text_latex: Two people, $P$ and $Q$, decide to independently roll two identical dice, each with 6 faces, numbered 1 to 6. The person with the higher number wins. In case both get the same number, they repeat the roll until someone wins. The probability that the game concludes on the third roll is \_\_\_\_\_\_\. (Answer in 3 decimal places)

questions.question_text:
Let G be a finite group on 84 elements. The size of a largest possible proper subgroup of G
is ________.
questions.explaination: By Lagrange's Theorem, the order of any subgroup $H$ of a finite group $G$ must divide $|G| = 84$. A proper subgroup cannot equal the whole group, so $|H| < 84$. The largest proper divisor of 84 is $\frac{84}{2} = 42$.

questions.question_text:
The postorder traversal of a binary tree is 8,9,6,7,4,5,2,3,1. The inorder traversal of the same
tree is 8,6,9,4,7,2,5,1,3. The height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root to
any leaf. The height of the binary tree above is ______.
questions.subtopic: Trees, binary search trees, binary heaps
questions.explaination: In postorder traversal, the root is the last element (1). Splitting inorder $[8,6,9,4,7,2,5]$ and $[3]$ around root 1 gives left subtree nodes and right subtree node 3. Recursively constructing the unique binary tree reveals the longest leaf path: $1 \to 2 \to 4 \to 6 \to 8$ (or 9), which has 4 edges. Thus, the height in terms of edges is 4.

questions.question_text:
A 32-bit wide main memory unit with a capacity of 1 GB is built using 256M × 4-bit DRAM
chips. The number of rows of memory cells in the DRAM chip is 214. The time taken to
perform one refresh operation is 50 nanoseconds. The refresh period is 2 milliseconds. The
percentage (rounded to the closest integer) of the time available for performing the memory
read/write operations in the main memory unit is __________.
questions.subtopic: Memory hierarchy: cache, main memory and secondary storage
questions.explaination: The DRAM has $2^{14} = 16384$ rows. Refreshing all rows takes $16384 \times 50\text{ ns} = 819.2\ \mu\text{s}$ every $2000\ \mu\text{s}$. The refresh overhead fraction is $\frac{819.2}{2000} = 40.96\%$. Hence, the percentage of time available for reading and writing memory is $100\% - 40.96\% = 59.04\% \approx 59\%$.
questions.question_text_latex: A 32-bit wide main memory unit with a capacity of 1 GB is built using $256\text{M} \times 4\text{-bit}$ DRAM chips. The number of rows of memory cells in the DRAM chip is $2^{14}$. The time taken to perform one refresh operation is 50 nanoseconds. The refresh period is 2 milliseconds. The percentage of time that the memory is available for performing the normal read and write operations is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\%. (Answer in integer)

questions.question_text:
Consider a system with 3 processes that share 4 instances of the same resource type. Each
process can request a maximum of 𝐾 instances. Resource instances can be requested and
released only one at a time. The largest value of 𝐾 that will always avoid deadlock is ____.
questions.explaination: For $n$ processes sharing $m$ instances of a single resource type where each process needs at most $K$ instances, deadlock is guaranteed to be avoided if $\sum_{i=1}^n (K - 1) < m \implies n(K - 1) \le m - 1$. Here $n = 3$ and $m = 4$, so $3(K - 1) \le 3 \implies K - 1 \le 1 \implies K \le 2$.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a system with 3 processes that share 4 instances of the same resource type. Each process can request at most $K$ instances of the resource type at any time. The largest value of $K$ that will always avoid deadlock is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

questions.question_text:
Consider a long-lived TCP session with an end-to-end bandwidth of 1 Gbps (= 109 bits-per-
second). The session starts with a sequence number of 1234. The minimum time (in seconds,
rounded to the closest integer) before this sequence number can be used again is _______.
questions.subtopic: Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
questions.explaination: A 32-bit sequence number space contains $2^{32} = 4{,}294{,}967{,}296$ bytes. At a transmission rate of $1\text{ Gbps} = \frac{10^9}{8} = 1.25 \times 10^8\text{ bytes/s}$, the wrap-around time is $\frac{2^{32}}{1.25 \times 10^8} = \frac{4294967296}{125000000} \approx 34.36$ seconds $\approx 34$ seconds.
questions.question_text_latex: Consider a 1 Gbps network with an MTU of 1500 bytes and a 32-bit sequence number space. The minimum time (in seconds, rounded to the nearest integer) after which the sequence numbers can wrap around is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.
